name: ParaSwap / Velora API Vocabulary
description: Key domain terms and concepts used in the ParaSwap (Velora) DEX aggregator APIs.

terms.definition: A service that sources liquidity from multiple decentralized exchanges (DEXes) simultaneously to find the best available swap rate for a given token pair and amount.

The optimal path for swapping one token to another, including all intermediate hops, DEX allocations, gas estimates, and USD valuations. Returned by /prices and must be passed unmodified to /transactions.
ParaSwap's smart contract router (named after Augustus, the Roman emperor) that executes token swaps on-chain. Referenced by contractAddress in the PriceRoute.
A smart contract that handles ERC-20 token approvals. Users approve this address (not the Augustus router) to transfer their tokens.
A swap where the user specifies the exact amount of source token to spend. The destination amount is variable.
A swap where the user specifies the exact amount of destination token to receive. The source amount is variable.
Hash-based Message Authentication Code appended to the PriceRoute to prevent tampering. The API validates this when /transactions is called.
The acceptable difference (in basis points) between the expected and actual swap price. 100 basis points = 1%. Used to protect users from price movement between quoting and execution.
Boolean flag set to true when the estimated price impact of the swap exceeds the configured maximum threshold (typically around 15%). Swaps may still be executable but carry high slippage risk.
When the bestRoute array contains multiple entries, the swap volume is split across different DEX paths to achieve better pricing through reduced price impact.
An EIP-2612 off-chain signature that authorizes token spending without a separate on-chain approval transaction, reducing gas costs.
A protocol-level fee (in basis points) that dApp integrators can charge on top of swaps. Configured via the partner and partnerFeePercent parameters.
Maximal Extractable Value protection. The Delta API provides MEV protection by using the Portikus Intents network where multiple agents compete to execute swaps off-chain before settlement.
An EIP-712 signed intent (not an on-chain transaction) submitted to the Delta API for gas-less swap execution. Competing agents (fillers) claim the best execution and settle on-chain.
ParaSwap's on-chain limit order and Request-for-Quote system that allows market makers to provide signed firm quotes for token pairs via a standardized HTTP API.
The intent-based execution network used by the Delta API where multiple solvers compete to fill user swap orders at the best price.
Ethereum Virtual Machine. ParaSwap supports 12 EVM-compatible chains including Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, and Avalanche.
Numeric identifier for a blockchain network. Ethereum Mainnet = 1, Polygon = 137, BNB Chain = 56. Used as path and query parameters throughout the API.
The array of optimal swap routes computed by ParaSwap's algorithm across all integrated DEXes, representing the path that maximizes the output amount.
The estimated cost of executing the swap transaction in USD terms, accounting for the current gas price and ETH/gas token market price.
